newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: DMCI Holdings shrugs off property fears.
newsitem.headline: DMCI Holdings shrugs off property fears.

text.p: DMCI Holdings Inc of the Philippines said on Wednesday it expected to get more construction projects this year despite fears of a glut in the local property market.

The country's largest builder of high-rise buildings had identified 19 billion pesos ($722.4 million) worth of potential construction contracts this year compared with 7.34 billion pesos last year, president Isidro Consunji said.
As at the end of the first quarter, DMCI's construction job orders reached 9.5 billion pesos, Consunji told shareholders during an annual meeting.

This figure does not include its contracts for the construction of five high-rise towers worth six billion pesos in the Rockwell development project in Manila's financial district of Makati and another project worth 1.1 billion pesos for Belle Corp.
DMCI also recently clinched a contract worth two billion pesos to do civil works for a 42-storey building for local firm Moldex, officials said.

"The perception of oversupply two to three years down the road are on the high- rise offices in particular and high-end residential. (But) there is no physical oversupply right now," Consunji said at a news conference after the meeting.
Speculation the Philippine property sector was heading for a crash has triggered industry-wide selling of property stocks in recent weeks. It eventually affected the whole bourse.

DMCI on Wednesday reported net income of 252 million pesos in the first quarter compared with 167 million in the previous period. It made net income of 1.05 billion pesos in 1996 from 494 million pesos in 1995.
Chief finance officer Herbert Consunji said construction of high-rise buildings accounted for 21 percent of the total 9.5 billion pesos worth of job orders booked in the first quarter.
But DMCI was confident it would be able to shift its business tack in the event of a glut in high-rise buildings.
"If the high-end won't move, we might have to refocus our efforts," its president said.
DMCI plans to invest more on infrastructure, industrial and low- to middle-income housing projects, he said.

The firm has 40 percent equity in a consortium that won a 25-year franchise to improve and manage water and sewerage facilities in the northern Philippine city of Olongapo which includes the Subic freeport. Project work began last month.
Among other projects, DMCI recently acquired 66 percent equity in Semirara Coal Corp which has a 15-year coal supply contract with state-owned National Power Corp.
DMCI is also scouting a partner for its planned $250 million cement plant which will use limestone mined by Semirara in central Philippines. ($1-26.30 pesos)
